items.summary: International observation systems reveal a consequential possibility: scientific information can be generated, validated, and circulated across institutional and political boundaries without requiring a single authority over all observations or a uniform distribution of capacities . Yet the existence of data-sharing protocols does not by itself establish shared understanding, mutual trust, legitimate reuse, or equitable participation in the production of knowledge . This discussion paper investigates the technical, epistemic, and institutional conditions under which global observation and knowledge infrastructures might be constructed and sustained . Drawing on meteorological and oceanographic cooperation, it distinguishes observational coverage, data availability, interoperability, interpretation, and collective authority. It proposes a preliminary federated research architecture connecting situated observation nodes, provenance and quality records, semantic and model translation, distributed computation, access governance, correction, and contestation. It treats mathematical, physical, social, and normative languages as historically formed manifestations and practices within generative-relational systems, distinguishing their conditional formal invariance from claims to universally identical representation. It further investigates why actors situated in different generative and institutional histories may interpret shared evidence differently, and proposes a bounded research vocabulary for mutually workable norms, continued disagreement, and rule revision without assuming epistemic consensus. The paper conceptualizes trust as a historically constituted relation supported in part by verifiable commitments, reciprocal inquiry, accountable institutions, and effective remedy rather than as a property supplied by cryptography or open data alone. It further specifies prospective services for common knowledge creation and circulation, generalized translation of heterogeneous generative-relational contexts, and traceable transformations of distinct forms of value. A staged validation design differentiates synthetic policy gates, cross-node scientific comparison, productive-capacity trials, and site-dependent ecological and institutional review. A cross-layer assessment profile separates technical interchange, scientific warrant, claimed competent authority, and effective contestation, without deriving legal or ethical legitimacy from technical success. It also examines epistemic and infrastructural asymmetries, the sensitivity of ecological and community data, the incompleteness of model-based assimilation, and the risks of concentrating interpretive authority in highly capable AI systems. Global weather and ocean observation provide instructive but bounded cases, not evidence that all knowledge should be made public or placed under centralized control. The proposed programme remains exploratory and separates conceptual architecture from implemented infrastructure, independent empirical assessment, and normative justification.
items.title: Global Observation and Knowledge Infrastructures: A Study of Collective Inquiry across Heterogeneous Relational Systems

items.summary: Spatial Methods Workbench is a citation-aware R Shiny environment with 12 guided workflows for spatial autocorrelation, conditional networks, spatially adjusted 2D and 3D networks, spatially varying networks, prediction, clustering, image-regression screening, mediation, and statistical shape analysis. Version 0.4.0 re-targets the three advanced network paths to the current public engines. The ISPat 2D and ISPat 3D paths call the CRAN package ISPAT3D 0.3.1 ( ispat3d_fit_2d for the section-wise planar fit and ispat3d_fit for the pooled volumetric fit: Matern-3/2 Vecchia Gaussian-process adjustment on spatially balanced anchors followed by a shared-plus-zone factor covariance fitted by Gaussian maximum likelihood, reported as signed zone partial correlations). The GP-GHS path calls GPGHS 1.0.1 ( gpghs_graph ) with the shrinkage-factor selection rule and AND symmetry of the accompanying article, and returns the GPGHS edge table with scores and signs. The retired ISPAT 0.1.0, ISPAT3D 0.1.1, and GPGHS 0.1.0 interfaces targeted by v0.3.1 no longer exist upstream. New controls expose factor rank, anchor budget, Vecchia neighbors, optimizer iterations, section handling, threads, and seeds; readiness checks require at least two zones with more rows than markers; result manifests record the engine package, version, and function; and real adapter smoke tests run whenever the engines are installed. Exact engine calls, built-in adaptations, and related screening workflows remain explicitly distinguished. items.summary: This dataset is the supplementary material for the manuscript "Decision Neutrality of Forecast Revisions in Microgrids with Photovoltaics and Battery Storage" by Yun Xing (Hohai University), submitted to Applied Sciences (MDPI). Version 1.0, 25 October 2026. Overview The study asks when adopting a revised next-day forecast changes a battery dispatch decision, rather than only the predicted cost. It derives two checkable sufficient reset conditions under which old and revised forecasts produce next-day storage value functions that differ only by an additive constant. A fixed-input perturbation bound separates this local neutrality from realized rolling-policy performance. Five policies (FF, FS, SF, SS and DAY) are compared on 522 community-days from 270 measured households aggregated into nine synthetic communities, with three synthetic tariffs and two import regimes. Key results - Freezing next-day forecasts is numerically neutral under unlimited imports across the tested tariffs. - Under a 30 kW import cap and time-of-use pricing, retaining midnight targets (DAY) lowers total operating cost by 3.105% relative to full updating (FF). Lower unmet-demand penalties account for 88.3% of the reduction; the import-bill reduction is 0.588%. - Freezing both forecasts while replanning (SS) costs 0.054% more than FF under the same six-hour replanning schedule, separating forecast adoption from target retention. - Under the same cap and tariff, freezing only the next-day forecast (FS) costs 0.188% more than FF. - Matched-calendar comparisons show that the magnitude of update effects depends on the controller scheme. items.summary: Multimodal $ΔΔG$ predictors integrating protein language models with inverse-folding representations achieve strong in-distribution accuracy on the Megascale dataset but exhibit limited robustness on out-of-distribution (OOD) proteins, persistent forward-reverse bias on paired-mutation benchmarks, and under-representation of rare stabilizing mutations. Existing approaches address these limitations primarily through additional architectural components, leaving optimization-level intervention comparatively underexplored. We introduce a constraint-aware optimization framework combining Balanced Mean Squared Error, a Siamese anti-symmetric regularizer, and a novel OOD-margin consistency loss on the per-position feature representation, requiring no architectural changes to the SPURS backbone. Across eleven benchmarks and three random seeds, the framework improves Spearman correlation on S669 from 0.486 to 0.540 ($σ=0.002$ across seeds), matching the published SPURS baseline (0.50) without architectural modification, and on S461 from 0.653 to 0.711, with consistent smaller gains on five additional OOD datasets. A controlled diagnostic on Ssym reveals that anti-symmetric training does not eliminate systematic forward-reverse bias, indicating that gains arise through implicit regularization rather than exact thermodynamic constraint enforcement.

items.summary: Multimodal $ΔΔG$ predictors integrating protein language models with inverse-folding representations achieve strong in-distribution accuracy on the Megascale dataset but exhibit limited robustness on out-of-distribution (OOD) proteins, persistent forward-reverse bias on paired-mutation benchmarks, and under-representation of rare stabilizing mutations. Existing approaches address these limitations primarily through additional architectural components, leaving optimization-level intervention comparatively underexplored. We introduce a constraint-aware optimization framework combining Balanced Mean Squared Error, a Siamese anti-symmetric regularizer, and a novel OOD-margin consistency loss on the per-position feature representation, requiring no architectural changes to the SPURS backbone. Across eleven benchmarks and three random seeds, the framework improves Spearman correlation on S669 from 0.486 to 0.540 ($σ=0.002$ across seeds), matching the published SPURS baseline (0.50) without architectural modification, and on S461 from 0.653 to 0.711, with consistent smaller gains on five additional OOD datasets. A controlled diagnostic on Ssym reveals that anti-symmetric training does not eliminate systematic forward-reverse bias, indicating that gains arise through implicit regularization rather than exact thermodynamic constraint enforcement.
items.title: Constraint-Aware Optimization for Robust Protein Stability Prediction

items.summary: Related: Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels , accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? Version of record: SSRN 7653679 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7653679 . Cite that version. The same text is also at polyhelper.ai/research/sealed-before-the-open/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/sealed-before-the-open . The registered predictions of Section 8 are on OSF: 10.17605/OSF.IO/9Q86N . The immutable release of the open league files on which every number of the paper rests: 10.5281/zenodo.23552700 . The live league and its open data (CC BY 4.0): trends.polyhelper.ai/markets , trends.polyhelper.ai/api/v1 . This deposit is an archival copy made so that the full text stays retrievable; it makes no separate claim. When an AI model says gold will rise, anyone can score the call at the close, but few can check when it was made. A backtest mixes memory with skill, and an operator's log asks for trust. I propose a standard for measuring AI market forecasts, written as a ladder of checkable requirements, and I run its reference implementation, AI Council · Markets: an open league where fourteen models, seven from US and seven from Chinese laboratories, face one question on one price snapshot. Before each New York open the ten on its Council, five from each side, give probabilities for twelve indicators at four horizons. Each answer is sealed into a hash chain before the price it is scored from, the chain is anchored in Bitcoin and signed by independent time-stamping authorities, and one run per session counts by a rule declared in advance. On 21 October 2026, the first counted morning, every counted answer was signed before the 09:30 ET open. Agreement among the models proved to be a count of independent voices, not a headcount: on two development mornings the seven and eight models sealed before the open were as alike as about 1.6 independent forecasters, nine counted ones were worth 2.23, and the closest pairs crossed the US-China line. Check a seal with three commands, and score my thirty predictions, registered on OSF, before I do.
items.title: Sealed Before the Open: A Verifiable Standard for Measuring AI Forecasts of Financial Markets

items.summary: International observation systems reveal a consequential possibility: scientific information can be generated, validated, and circulated across institutional and political boundaries without requiring a single authority over all observations or a uniform distribution of capacities . Yet the existence of data-sharing protocols does not by itself establish shared understanding, mutual trust, legitimate reuse, or equitable participation in the production of knowledge . This discussion paper investigates the technical, epistemic, and institutional conditions under which global observation and knowledge infrastructures might be constructed and sustained . Drawing on meteorological and oceanographic cooperation, it distinguishes observational coverage, data availability, interoperability, interpretation, and collective authority. It proposes a preliminary federated research architecture connecting situated observation nodes, provenance and quality records, semantic and model translation, distributed computation, access governance, correction, and contestation. It treats mathematical, physical, social, and normative languages as historically formed manifestations and practices within generative-relational systems, distinguishing their conditional formal invariance from claims to universally identical representation. It further investigates why actors situated in different generative and institutional histories may interpret shared evidence differently, and proposes a bounded research vocabulary for mutually workable norms, continued disagreement, and rule revision without assuming epistemic consensus. The paper conceptualizes trust as a historically constituted relation supported in part by verifiable commitments, reciprocal inquiry, accountable institutions, and effective remedy rather than as a property supplied by cryptography or open data alone. It further specifies prospective services for common knowledge creation and circulation, generalized translation of heterogeneous generative-relational contexts, and traceable transformations of distinct forms of value. A staged validation design differentiates synthetic policy gates, cross-node scientific comparison, productive-capacity trials, and site-dependent ecological and institutional review. A cross-layer assessment profile separates technical interchange, scientific warrant, claimed competent authority, and effective contestation, without deriving legal or ethical legitimacy from technical success. It also examines epistemic and infrastructural asymmetries, the sensitivity of ecological and community data, the incompleteness of model-based assimilation, and the risks of concentrating interpretive authority in highly capable AI systems. Global weather and ocean observation provide instructive but bounded cases, not evidence that all knowledge should be made public or placed under centralized control. The proposed programme remains exploratory and separates conceptual architecture from implemented infrastructure, independent empirical assessment, and normative justification.
items.title: Global Observation and Knowledge Infrastructures: A Study of Collective Inquiry across Heterogeneous Relational Systems

items.summary: Spatial Methods Workbench is a citation-aware R Shiny environment with 12 guided workflows for spatial autocorrelation, conditional networks, spatially adjusted 2D and 3D networks, spatially varying networks, prediction, clustering, image-regression screening, mediation, and statistical shape analysis. Version 0.4.0 re-targets the three advanced network paths to the current public engines. The ISPat 2D and ISPat 3D paths call the CRAN package ISPAT3D 0.3.1 ( ispat3d_fit_2d for the section-wise planar fit and ispat3d_fit for the pooled volumetric fit: Matern-3/2 Vecchia Gaussian-process adjustment on spatially balanced anchors followed by a shared-plus-zone factor covariance fitted by Gaussian maximum likelihood, reported as signed zone partial correlations). The GP-GHS path calls GPGHS 1.0.1 ( gpghs_graph ) with the shrinkage-factor selection rule and AND symmetry of the accompanying article, and returns the GPGHS edge table with scores and signs. The retired ISPAT 0.1.0, ISPAT3D 0.1.1, and GPGHS 0.1.0 interfaces targeted by v0.3.1 no longer exist upstream. New controls expose factor rank, anchor budget, Vecchia neighbors, optimizer iterations, section handling, threads, and seeds; readiness checks require at least two zones with more rows than markers; result manifests record the engine package, version, and function; and real adapter smoke tests run whenever the engines are installed. This complete source distribution contains the installable Workbench package, Shiny application, five executable vignettes, compact simulated datasets, complete documentation, automated checks, and locally bundled package sources for the exact CRAN ISPAT3D 0.3.1 and GPGHS 1.0.1 engines. install-complete.R installs those local engine copies and the single compiled dependency gpboost without cloning their repositories. A curated public-source bundle also preserves license-safe regression, clustering, neural, SV-NN, STCAR, and SBLF source connected to the Workbench adaptations and related-method provenance. Exact engine calls, built-in adaptations, and related screening workflows remain explicitly distinguished. Large curriculum translations, media, Git history, and platform-specific compiled objects are omitted because they do not execute a Workbench analysis. Installation Download and extract the release, then run Rscript install-complete.R , Rscript verify-installation.R , and Rscript tests/testthat.R . items.summary: Background/Objectives : With the advent of the current digital health age, opportunities for interacting with health systems have grown not only more frequent but also variable in type, spanning across emergent care settings, routine outpatient follow-up, as well as at-home telemedicine-based platforms. In light of initiatives to re-design electronic medical records (EMR) to more meaningfully curate evidence-based insights, our research objective is focused on harnessing underutilized data features (i.e., time-ordered events) to map the complex interactions that patients undergo within their health systems. We posit that inclusion of information associated with sequential patterns will help more accurately simulate care pathways and outcomes. We report preliminary data on care utilization patterns among cohorts of patients diagnosed with chronic disease. Methods : De-identified data were extracted from the MedStar Health AIM-AHEAD Data Bridge (AADB)’s Chronic Disease repository. EMRs were queried for patients with confirmed diagnoses for diabetes mellitus (ICD-10: E10.X or E11.X) as well as heart failure (ICD-10: I50.X). For each unique patient, encounters related to care utilization were sequentially collated, with explicit demarcation of whether interactions occurred before or after corresponding diagnoses. For analytical purposes, encounters were categorized as “Emergency”, “Inpatient”, “Observation”, “Outpatient”, “Home Health”, and “Patient Portal”. For each cohort, sequential pattern mining (SPM) was used to generate antecedent-consequent prediction rules and calculate the conditional probabilities (confidence) of subsequent care utilization episodes. Analyses were performed using R (The R Foundation for Statistical Computing; version 4.5.2). Results : Between January 2018 and December 2024, we distinctly identified 202,605 patients with a diagnosis for diabetes mellitus as well as 79,223 patients with a diagnosis for heart failure. Across both cohorts, 42,208 patients had documentation of being diagnosed with both conditions and were flagged separately for potential sensitivity analyses. The proportion of older patients (50 years or above) was predominant (>85% for all patients). We expect to enrich our data pipeline with more detailed clinical features (e.g., medications, laboratory panels, procedures) in future iterations. This comprehensive ingestion would enable the initial steps towards developing models for predicting the onset of unfavorable health outcomes. items.summary: This dataset is the supplementary material for the manuscript "Decision Neutrality of Forecast Revisions in Microgrids with Photovoltaics and Battery Storage" by Yun Xing (Hohai University), submitted to Applied Sciences (MDPI). Version 1.0, 25 October 2026. Overview The study asks when adopting a revised next-day forecast changes a battery dispatch decision, rather than only the predicted cost. It derives two checkable sufficient reset conditions under which old and revised forecasts produce next-day storage value functions that differ only by an additive constant. A fixed-input perturbation bound separates this local neutrality from realized rolling-policy performance. Five policies (FF, FS, SF, SS and DAY) are compared on 522 community-days from 270 measured households aggregated into nine synthetic communities, with three synthetic tariffs and two import regimes. Key results - Freezing next-day forecasts is numerically neutral under unlimited imports across the tested tariffs. - Under a 30 kW import cap and time-of-use pricing, retaining midnight targets (DAY) lowers total operating cost by 3.105% relative to full updating (FF). Lower unmet-demand penalties account for 88.3% of the reduction; the import-bill reduction is 0.588%. - Freezing both forecasts while replanning (SS) costs 0.054% more than FF under the same six-hour replanning schedule, separating forecast adoption from target retention. - Under the same cap and tariff, freezing only the next-day forecast (FS) costs 0.188% more than FF. - Matched-calendar comparisons show that the magnitude of update effects depends on the controller scheme. items.summary: International observation systems reveal a consequential possibility: scientific information can be generated, validated, and circulated across institutional and political boundaries without requiring a single authority over all observations or a uniform distribution of capacities . Yet the existence of data-sharing protocols does not by itself establish shared understanding, mutual trust, legitimate reuse, or equitable participation in the production of knowledge . This discussion paper investigates the technical, epistemic, and institutional conditions under which global observation and knowledge infrastructures might be constructed and sustained . Drawing on meteorological and oceanographic cooperation, it distinguishes observational coverage, data availability, interoperability, interpretation, and collective authority. It proposes a preliminary federated research architecture connecting situated observation nodes, provenance and quality records, semantic and model translation, distributed computation, access governance, correction, and contestation. It treats mathematical, physical, social, and normative languages as historically formed manifestations and practices within generative-relational systems, distinguishing their conditional formal invariance from claims to universally identical representation. It further investigates why actors situated in different generative and institutional histories may interpret shared evidence differently, and proposes a bounded research vocabulary for mutually workable norms, continued disagreement, and rule revision without assuming epistemic consensus. The paper conceptualizes trust as a historically constituted relation supported in part by verifiable commitments, reciprocal inquiry, accountable institutions, and effective remedy rather than as a property supplied by cryptography or open data alone. It further specifies prospective services for common knowledge creation and circulation, generalized translation of heterogeneous generative-relational contexts, and traceable transformations of distinct forms of value. A staged validation design differentiates synthetic policy gates, cross-node scientific comparison, productive-capacity trials, and site-dependent ecological and institutional review. A cross-layer assessment profile separates technical interchange, scientific warrant, claimed competent authority, and effective contestation, without deriving legal or ethical legitimacy from technical success. It also examines epistemic and infrastructural asymmetries, the sensitivity of ecological and community data, the incompleteness of model-based assimilation, and the risks of concentrating interpretive authority in highly capable AI systems. Global weather and ocean observation provide instructive but bounded cases, not evidence that all knowledge should be made public or placed under centralized control. The proposed programme remains exploratory and separates conceptual architecture from implemented infrastructure, independent empirical assessment, and normative justification.
